Region: Northern Mediterranean coast, from Carmel toward Tyre and Sidon
History: Asher was Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His name means happy, and Jacob blessed him with rich food and royal delicacies (Genesis 49:20). Asher's allotment ran along the northern coast, but the tribe never drove out the Canaanites of its towns (Judges 1:31-32) and lived among them. Asher is the quietest tribe in the history: it appears in the census lists and in the blessing of Moses (Deuteronomy 33:24-25), and Anna the prophetess, who recognised the infant Jesus in the temple, was of the tribe of Asher (Luke 2:36). The tribe was deported with the northern kingdom.
Culture: Asher's culture was coastal: farming the fertile plain, trading with the Phoenician cities to its north, and living alongside Canaanite neighbours its armies never displaced.
Religion: Asher shared Israel's worship of the LORD, though living among Canaanite towns exposed it to the idolatry the conquest was meant to remove.
BibleConnection: Asher's story is one of quiet persistence: a tribe that never produced a judge or a king, yet is named among the sealed in Revelation 7 and gives the New Testament its aged prophetess Anna.
